name: ffuf
plain: `ffuf` replaces the word FUZZ in a request with every line of a wordlist and shows which answers look interesting. FUZZ can sit in the path, a parameter, a header, a cookie or a POST body.

That one idea covers directory discovery, parameter discovery, virtual host discovery and simple login guessing. The skill is in filtering: most guesses give the same boring reply, so you hide it by status (-fc), size (-fs), words (-fw) or lines (-fl) and look at what is left.
when: Find virtual hosts by changing the Host header.
Test many values in a field with a filter on the response.

examples.title: Directory discovery
examples.explain: FUZZ in the URL is replaced with each word. Results print with status, size, words and lines.

examples.title: Hide the common reply
examples.explain: -fc hides a status code and -fs hides a response size. If every wrong guess is 1234 bytes, hiding that size leaves only the real hits.

examples.title: Add extensions
examples.explain: -e tries each word with each extension too.

examples.title: Find virtual hosts
examples.explain: FUZZ goes in the Host header. A different size from the default means a different site.

examples.title: Fuzz a parameter name
examples.explain: Finds which parameter changes the page; many hidden pages react to ?debug= or ?file=.

examples.title: Fuzz a parameter value
examples.explain: A numbered list of ids shows which exist. Process substitution <(seq 1 200) builds the list on the fly.

examples.title: POST login guessing in a lab
examples.explain: -fr hides replies matching a regular expression (here the failure message). The reply that is different is the match.

examples.title: Two wordlists at once
examples.explain: Name each list with :NAME and use that name in the request to try all combinations.

examples.title: Save as a file
examples.explain: -o and -of write results as json, csv, html and more.

options.plain: Target URL, with FUZZ marking the spot.
Wordlist, optionally with a keyword name (default FUZZ).
Add a header; can hold FUZZ.
Match by size, word count, line count or regex.
Filter out by size, word count, line count or regex.
Replay only the matched requests to a proxy.
Verbose: print full URL and redirect.
Stop on spurious errors or on all errors.
Ignore comment lines in the wordlist.
Run a command to produce the input.

mistakes: Not filtering: a thousand lines of the same reply hide the one that matters. Try -ac or -fs.
Forgetting to quote a URL with & or ? in the shell.
Wrong keyword when you use two lists.
Too many threads on a small server.
Fuzzing a real site without permission.
try: Find a hidden directory with common.txt and -fc 404.
Find the response size of a wrong guess, then filter it with -fs.
Try Host: FUZZ.target.htb on a lab machine.
see_also: gobuster(1), wfuzz(1), curl(1), burpsuite, and the seclists wordlists in /usr/share/seclists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
